title: Select Binding
content: ### **Objective** Edit Binding Properties. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Binding ▶ **Select Binding** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Select Binding ** **※Note:** 3D toolbar ▶ Select bindings with the Select/Move tool. ** Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated.** **→ The line segment for which the binding was created is displayed. 2. Select the Binding to be edited. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Configure each property as needed referring to below table. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Rename Binding's name. **Line Length** | Check Binding's length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. **Type**** ** | **Under** | Bindings are placed under the Patterns to express Inside Bindings. **Over ** | Bindings are placed over the Patterns. **Both (ver 7.0)** | Bindings are placed both direction of the Patterns. **Dimension** | **Width** | Adjust selected Binding's width. (1~50mm) **Length ** | Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50% ~ 200%) or a specific value. **Particle Distance** | Edit selected Binding's [Particle Distance](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000414447-Particle-Distance-Setting-) (4~20mm) **Add'l Thickness - Collision** | Adjust Binding's[ Add'l Thickness - Collision](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002798068-Adjust-Collision-Thickness). **Fabric** | Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the [Fabric Object Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000714287-FABRIC) appear in a list. **Grain Direction**** ** | Bias/ Warp/ Custom | Choose among Bias, Warp, or Custom for the Binding's grain direction. Angle | Manually insert Angle value to set the Binding's grain direction. **Topstitch ** | Add Topstitch to the Binding. The Topstitch option shows the styles which are added in the Topstitch tab of Object Browser. [**Sewing Line Type**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000496627--Property-Sewing-Line-Type) | Edit Binding's Sewing Line Type. **Extend ** | Set whether to extend the binding after creating it on a part of the line segment. **※ Note:** Binding Extension is not possible in the following cases. When the angle of both segments are more than 180 degrees based on the binding start/end point. 4. Right-click on the Binding to be edited. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete selected Binding. **Reset Arrangement** | Reset Binding's position. Use this option to fix unstable simulations. **Deactivate / Activate** | Deactivate or activate selected Binding. **Freeze / Unfreeze** | Freeze or unfreeze selected Binding. **Flip Normal ** | The selected Binding's face flips to the other side.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing binding properties within the software, detailing steps, options, and configurations available in the Property Editor.

title: Fabric_Color
content: **List of Contents** Color Change color Change color with Eyedropper **Color** \- Change the color of the fabric. ** Change Color** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BaLA0rWayII \- When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected item’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. \- Click on the Color chip to open the Color window to assign the desired Color to the selected item. \- Click the desired Color. The selected Color will be applied to the item. \- Click OK to complete. **Change Color with Eyedropper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bYoJXtoD0VE \- When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected item’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. \- Click on the Color chip to open the Color window. \- Select the **Eyedropper** tool. \- Drag the mouse cursor outside the Color window. When the cursor changes to an Eyedropper, click on the spot anywhere in the window to extract the desired color. \- The color of the selected spot will appear in the Color window. \- Select OK to complete. \- The chosen Color will be assigned to the selected item. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover how to effortlessly change the color of your design elements using the Property Editor and the Eyedropper tool with our step-by-step guide and helpful videos.

title: How to redeem my discount?
content: **Redemption Eligibility Note:** Please be advised that this promotion is strictly reserved for individuals who have received and finalized the official CLO Public Workshop Survey. Verification of survey participation is required to qualify for this subscription discount. Thank you for participating in our workshop survey; your insights are invaluable to our team. To claim your 20% discount on your next CLO subscription, please submit an inquiry via our Contact Us page. Ensure you provide the following verification and account details: * Survey Email: Specify the exact email address used for the survey submission to facilitate verification. * CLO Account Email: Designate the CLO account for discount application (this may differ from the survey email address provided). * Subscription Plan: Clearly indicate your preferred subscription plan (monthly or yearly). Once your survey submission has been verified, we will apply the corresponding discount to your designated CLO account. If you have any additional questions, please include them in your inquiry via the [**Contact Us**](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) page. We are happy to assist!

title: Automated Arrangement Point Creation
content: **Automated Arrangement Point Creation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9NPKXBmTUlQ \- Load an Avatar by navigating to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ. \- **Automatically Add Arrangement Points** option under Load OBJ window ▶ Load as Avatar is selected by default. \- Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes are automatically created sized to the loaded OBJ. **※Note****: ** This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. ‘Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose of A-pose’
content_description: This page provides a guide on using the Automated Arrangement Point Creation feature in a 3D modeling software, detailing the steps to import an OBJ file and automatically generate arrangement points for avatars in T or A poses.

title: Fabric Kit Manual
content: ## 1\. COMPONENTS ### **Please identify and confirm the following components.** ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054560874/mceclip0.png) ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054560894/mceclip1.png) **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)SCALE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)UTILITY KNIFE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)SCREWDRIVER** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)CHARGING ADAPTER** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)USER MANUAL** ## 2\. TOOL LEGEND ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png) **BENDING TEST DEVICE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561034/mceclip2.png)** ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png) **STRETCH TEST DEVICE** ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561014/mceclip0.png) ## 3\. SPECIFICATION ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561154/mceclip3.png) ## 4\. HOW TO ATTACH THE DIGITAL FORCE GAUGE TO THE FABRIC KIT ### **Use total of eight screws to assemble. Remaining two screws are extra.** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png)Screw the Jig into the Digital Force Gauge. Turn about 3-4 times and do not tighten all the way. However screw the Jig until the Control Lever faces up, aligning with the Digital Force Gauge.** **![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428853/mceclip4.png)** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png)Align the Holder underneath the Digital Force Gauge. ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Fasten the Holder to the Digital Force Gauge with Screws (x4). ** **![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561414/mceclip8.png)** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png)Loosely tighten the Screws (x4) to affix the Digital Force Gauge to the Fabric Kit, enough so that Digital Force Gauge can be moved.** **![mceclip10.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561454/mceclip10.png)** **![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429013/mceclip11.png) Shift the Digital Force Gauge to align the Jig as the image below vertically.** **![mceclip12.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561474/mceclip12.png)** **![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561494/mceclip13.png) Tighten Screw B to affix the Digital Force Gauge Holder to the Fabric Kit. ****If the Digital Force Gauge is not affixed properly, the measured Force values may not be accurate.** ## 5\. OVERVIEW **Prepare fabrics![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Measure the fabric weight and thickness ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Measure the bending strength ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Measure the stretch ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Calculate entered measurements ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Apply a texture** ## 6\. HOW TO MAKE FABRIC ### **Launch CLO Enterprise, then switch to Emulator mode using the top-right drop-down menu to enter the values measured from the Fabric Kit.** #### ** A. SWATCH PREPARATION ** **![mceclip17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429393/mceclip17.png)Before cutting out the swatches, please ironing the swatch gently without causing any shrinkage.** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Confirm the grainline of the fabric.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Prepare a total of three swatches with the provided stencil. ****** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png) Each swatch will represent a different grain, cut in the (1) weft, (2) warp, and (3) bias directions, measuring 220mm x 30mm in size.** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png) These will be used to measure the weight, bending, and stretch properties of the fabric.** **![mceclip16.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561774/mceclip16.png)** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Cut the swatches along the drawn guidelines, being as precise as possible for accurate measurements. ****** #### **B. FABRIC WEIGHT** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Turn on the scale.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Place all three swatches on the scale. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Enter the displayed weight in the Emulator. ** **![mceclip18.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561794/mceclip18.png)** #### **C. FABRIC THICKNESS** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Press the lever of the thickness gauge to create a gap and place the swatch.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Place the 220mm x 30mm swatch in between the gap. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Release the lever and enter the measured thickness to the Emulator. ** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png) Click Next to continue. ** **![mceclip19.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561834/mceclip19.png)** #### **D. BENDING TEST** **The Bending Test is performed 3 times : first for the weft swatch, and next the warp swatch, then the last for the bias swatch.** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Slide open the 1-1 Ruler of the Bending Test device.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Turn the 1-2 Clamp back, then insert the end of the swatch, lining it up to the dotted line. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Pull down the 1-2 Clamp to affix the swatch. ** **![mceclip20.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561914/mceclip20.png)** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png) Wind the 1-4 Control Lever clockwise, then stop when the fabric hits the ground. ** **![mceclip21.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429453/mceclip21.png)** **![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429013/mceclip11.png) Measure and enter this point of contact as the Contact Distance (A). ** **![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561494/mceclip13.png) Place the 1-1 Ruler beneath the swatch, then enter the measured length (B) in the Emulator. ** **![mceclip22.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561954/mceclip22.png)** #### **E. STRETCH TEST** **The stretch test will allow you to measure the stretchability and threshold at which a fabric will no longer stretch. To do this you will explore the relationship between length of stretch and force applied to the fabric, then record and input your findings into the Emulator Mode of CLO.** **The reading from the Length Ruler and Digital Force Gauge combined will be one set of measurements. You will need a minimum of 3 sets and a maximum of 5 sets for each swatch.** **When testing, you will need to determine, which unit of length will be your constant.** ![mceclip23.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429513/mceclip23.png) **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Wind the Control Lever until the needle aligns with 0 on the Length Ruler.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Loosen the Clamps at each end of the Fabric Bed. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Insert both ends of the swatch between the Jig openings, aligning the 10mm line marks. ** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png) Tighten the Clamps at each end to secure the swatch ends.** **![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429013/mceclip11.png) Turn on the Digital Force Gauge. ****** **![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561494/mceclip13.png) Determine Length constant: ** **![mceclip17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429393/mceclip17.png) We recommend you to fill out all five sections as possible because when you have more measurements, data is more accurate.** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png)When the swatch is pulled by 1mm and the force is less than 0.01kgf** **1) Pull the fabric swatch until the force value is 0.01kgf. 2) Starting with the length reached at step 1, check the length and force of each 10mm increment. 3) Record 10 sections. (In the case of not being able to record 10 sections, record all the measurable sections.) 4) Use a value only when the force difference of each section is at least 0.02kgf. (If the force difference for each interval is less than 0.02kgf, do not use that value.) 5) Finally, select and use values resulted in at least 3 sections and up to 5 sections. (We recommend that you fill out all five sections as much as possible because the more measurements you have, the more accurate the data is.).** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png)When the swatch is pulled by 1 mm and the force value is over 0.01kgf** **1) Check the value of the force when the swatch is pulled to 1mm. 2) Starting with the length reached at step 1, check the length and force of each 1mm increments. 3) At this time, measure 3 to 5 sections. (We recommend that you ll out all ve sections as much as possible because the more measurements you have, the more accurate the data is)** **![mceclip24.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054563194/mceclip24.png) Once the test has been completed for a swatch, reset the Control Lever so the needle aligns with 0 on the Length Ruler. Then unscrew the clamp at each end and remove the swatch. If you are finished testing you can turn the Digital Force Gauge off. In between each swatch test you should turn the digital force gauge off and then back on after the needle has been returned to the 0 marks. ****** **![mceclip25.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429673/mceclip25.png) Click Next to Continue. ** ## 7\. HOW TO USE THE DIGITAL FORCE GAUGE **The Digital Force Gauge uses the default settings as the image below. If a button was mistakenly pushed, power the Digital Force Gauge off, then on, to reset the device to its default settings. However, if the default unit of measurement was changed, press button B to reset the device to Kgf.** **![mceclip27.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054563294/mceclip27.png)** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)FREQUENTLY USED BUTTONS** **A. POWER** \- **turn the Digital Force Gauge on/off** **C. LED - turn the LED display on/off** **D. UNIT - change the unit of measurement; Kgf is used to measure the stretch** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)FREQUENTLY USED BUTTONS** **The following buttons are not used in the Stretch Test.** **If one of these buttons are mistakenly pushed, reset the Digital Force Gauge with the Power button.** **B. RESET** **E. MODE** **F. REVIEW ****G. SETTINGS I. SAVE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)CHARGING** **Use the provided adapter to charge the Digital Force Gauge.**
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for identifying components, conducting fabric tests, and utilizing the Digital Force Gauge, ensuring accurate measurements for fabric properties.

title: Select/Move Point/Segment
content: **List of Contents** Select Move ### **Objective** Modify Patterns, Internal, and Base (ver5.2) Shapes by moving points and segments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012650767/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** **Operation** **Select** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012650767/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** 2. Click a point or segment of a Pattern or Internal Shape. → The point or segment is selected. → When there are multiple points or segments, a pop-up menu appears allowing you to select the desired one (ver3.0.0.) 3. To select multiple points and segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when clicking them. → All clicked points and segments are selected. 4. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass points and segments to be selected with the marquee box. → All points and segments inside the marquee box are selected. **Move** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037147)**Transform Pattern** 2. Click and drag the Pattern or use the [arrow keys](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000376767-%EB%B0%A9%ED%96%A5%ED%82%A4%EB%A1%9C-%EC%9D%B4%EB%8F%99). 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the point or segment. → The point or segment can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope.→ The center point of the dart is moved along the direction of the center line's tilt **(ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142637530649)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=mOQg7GggSZkBW3dn&t=2557)**)** 4. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the point or segment to type in distance moved. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Distance Moved** | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. **X-Axis (ver4.2.0)** | Type in how much a point is moved on x-axis. This option does not appear for segments. **Y-Axis (ver4.2.0)** | Type in how much a point is moved on Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. **※ Note:** If it is cumbersome to select Patterns using the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037167) **Edit Pattern** tool, use the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037147) **Transform Pattern** tool. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to modify patterns and shapes in CLO 3D by selecting and moving points and segments using the Edit and Transform tools.

title: Auto Sewing (ver 6.0)
content: **Objective** Patterns are automatically sewn based on their placement on avatars. **※Note:** The available range of automatic sewing is as follows, * Garment: * Top (T-shirts, jackets, Jumper, etc.) and One-piece are possible. * Bottom (Skirt, Pants, etc) and Pants are impossible. * Parts: Bodies, Sleeves, Collars, Darts, Pleats, Cuffs, Sleeves with Vend & Placket. * Layers: One-ply patterns such as Pockets and Lining except for two-layer Patterns. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ojB6NZU7q14 **Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Auto Sewing** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Auto Sewing** **Operation** 1. Click the [Arrangement Points ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001999287-Arrange-Pattern-with-Arrangement-Points-Flip-Wrap-Direction)of the Avatar to arrange the Pattern. Since Auto Sewing is calculated by the information of the Arrangement Points (where each Pattern Piece is arranged), correct Arrangement Points should be used based on the rules below, Otherwise, Auto Sewing may not work properly. (It is only applicable to the Bounding Volumes provided by CLO) **Collar/ Band** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's neck. ---|--- **Bodies** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's body. **Sleeves** | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's arm, the cuffs can be used either arm/wrist Arrangement Points. **Bottom (ver 6.1)** | Use Arrangement Points at the legs. **※Note:** Be mindful to arrange the pieces to auto sew correctly. \- If the belt length includes a placket which is placed over the zipper, arrange the placket piece. \- Trace the internal line of the side pocket along side seams. \- If the pants width is large, arrange front and back pattern pieces separately by using each of the arrangement points. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The arranged patterns are automatically sewn. **※Note:** * If sewing has been applied prior to automatic sewing, it is maintained while the rest of the sewing lines are being additionally auto-sewn. * Darts and Pleats can be sewn automatically without arranging patterns. * For Pleats, automatic sewing is possible only when Internal Lines are defined by the fold direction of the Pleats.
content_description: Explore the Auto Sewing feature to seamlessly arrange and automatically sew garment patterns on avatars, ensuring precise placement for optimal results.

title: [Property] 3D Seamline
content: ### **Objective** Adjust **Intensity** and **Thickness** of 3D seamlines to render a realistic Garment. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing ** 3D/2D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024256947/edit_sewing.png) **Edit Sewing** ** Operation ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Select a Sewing Line. → Properties of the Sewing Line appears in the Property Editor. 3. title: Create an Avatar Fitting Suit (ver 7.3)
content: **Objective** A fitting suit is an invisible component connected to an avatar that enables usage of the [re-drape feature](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034333873-Re-drape-3D-Arrangement-ver-5-1). CLO-native avatars include it by default, while it always has to be added for custom avatars. How to create a fitting suit: YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0?si=1r9hHwB45kw77gU2&start=1434 **Location** Main Menu▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor**▶ Fitting Suit** ** ****Operation** 1. Load the object to create the fitting suit. 2. Click the tool/menu indicated. → Fitting Suit window appears. 3. [Create the circumference line on](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055394453-Avatar-Measure-ver-6-0-) the avatar's position as the image. → The pattern of the fitting suit is displayed. → The circumference line on both sides are automatically created symmetrically. **※ Note:** You can create each by clicking the Symmetry button off at the top. 4. After creating all circumference line, click the Drape Fitting Suit button. → The fitting suit is draped. **※ Note:** * When you click the Auto-Create Fitting Suit button, the fitting suit is automatically created on your avatar. At this time, if the avatar is not created properly, we recommend creating it manually. * You can delete it by selecting the circumference line you want to delete from the avatar or by selecting the item in the fitting suit window and clicking the delete button. * You can return to the initial state by clicking the reset button.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on creating a fitting suit for avatars to utilize the re-drape feature in CLO, ensuring custom avatars achieve optimal fitting and draping quality.

title: Avatar IK Joint Mapping
content: ## **New in 2025.0** IK Joint Mapping Set T-Pose Open/Save #### Streamline IK joint mapping for various avatars to achieve natural movement while ensuring seamless compatibility for motions and poses across all avatars. The avatar must have properly defined joint points. Rigging must include key joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UvWChktL4ZU?si=hBC_fnvPaBX1VwUb #### #### **IK Joint Mapping** **ℹ️** The FBX file must not contain joints with duplicate names, and IK mapping may not apply correctly for creatures or quadruped avatars with non-human structures. 1\. Click Main Menu » Avatar » Avatar Editor » **IK Joint** tab. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163389593)** Joints are categorized into required and optional, and you must map all required joints to ensure proper IK setup. ![IK.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695503254809) For optional joints, we recommend mapping those indicated in the image if they are present in the avatar to achieve more accurate results. ![IK_Optional.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44698897617177) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163389593)** **Auto** If the avatar meets the following conditions, click **![Auto Mapping.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163400089)**at the top right to apply automatic mapping. • If each joint name of the avatar matches that of the CLO avatar. • If the avatar is from one of the following platforms: **Daz 3D, Adobe Mixamo, Reallusion Character Creator, or Unreal Engine MetaHuman.** **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163389593)** **Manual** 1. Click the desired item from the image or list in the IK Mapping tab, then click the joint to be mapped on the avatar. _* Alternatively, you can first click the joint on the avatar and then click an item from the tab._ 2. When ![IK Symmetric.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695147316505)**S****ymmetry Mapping** option at the top right is turned on, the corresponding joint on the opposite side is automatically mapped. Note that both sides must be named as follows: **Left_** / **Right_, L_ / R_** , **Left / Right** , **_L / _R** , **_Left / _Right. ** 3. Once all mapping is set up, adjust the [IK pose.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115009052548-Adjust-Avatar-Joints#h_01J90BEJ6RBW7SQZXTSHZZSA80) **✨Tip:** Use the following tips to enhance the motion quality on the target avatar after IK mapping. • Offset Joint: If a specific joint does not align properly, adjust the avatar joints by using [Offset Joint](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/39336772755737-Offset-Avatar-Joint). • Move to Ground: If the avatar is floating above the ground after applying a motion file, right-click on the avatar and click 'Move to Ground'. #### #### **Set T-Pose** Set the avatar in a T-pose to ensure proper compatibility with CLO avatar pose and motion files apply correctly. 1. Adjust the avatar’s joints directly to a T-pose using the gizmo in the 3D window. _If the avatar is already in a T-pose, this step can be skipped._ 2. Click **![Set T-Pose.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695147319449)** at the top right. **📝****Note:** • If set correctly, the ![Reset Pose.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44698897618329) button activates, allowing you to check the set T-pose when cilcked. • After adjusting the pose during IK mapping, click the Reset Pose button to revert the avatar to the set T-pose. #### #### **Open/Save** You can manage the IK data mapped to the avatar as a file. 1. Click ![Button-1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695147320473) **Save** / ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163440025)**Open** at the top right to open or save IK data as a _.iks_ file. * IK files are only compatible between avatars that have been mapped.
content_description: Discover the powerful new IK Joint Mapping features in 2025.0 that streamline avatar rigging for natural movement and seamless compatibility across diverse avatars.

title: How can I fix the 2GB file size limit error when saving?
content: ## **Question** When I try to save my project in CLO, a warning popup appears saying **"Files exceeding 2GB cannot be saved as a single ZPRJ file."** and I cannot save my file. How can I fix this problem and save my project? ## **Answer** The problem occurs when the total file size of your project exceeds the maximum limit (2GB) allowed for a single `.zprj` file in CLO. This is mainly caused by heavy animation recorded data or high-resolution texture files. To resolve this issue and successfully save your work, please check and try the two methods below: #### 1\. If the recorded animation data exceeds 2GB: If you have recorded a long animation, the data cached in the track can easily exceed 2GB. In this case, you can manually divide the animation into multiple files by cutting the layers. * **Step 1:** In the **Animation Editor** timeline, right-click on the specific frame time where you want to split the sequence. * **Step 2:** Click **'Cut Layer'** from the context menu to split the animation track. * **Step 3:** Separate and save the divided sequences into different project files (e.g., `z1.zprj`, `z2.zprj`, `z3.zprj`) so that each file stays under the 2GB limit. #### 2\. If multiple heavy texture files are applied to the garment: If your project contains multiple high-resolution graphics, heavy normal maps, or large background textures, the file size will increase drastically. * **Resize Textures:** Check the original file size of the images applied as textures. Open them in an image editor (like Photoshop) to lower the resolution or compress the file size before re-applying them to CLO.
content_description: This webpage provides solutions for users encountering a "Files exceeding 2GB cannot be saved as a single ZPRJ file" error in CLO, offering practical methods to manage project file sizes effectively.

title: Set View Control
content: **Objective** Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software becomes the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶**View Control** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **View Control** **※ Note: **A key and mouse control combination can be set for one function. If a combination is repeated, the interface may not work properly. **Preset** | Select one of the default presets. ---|--- **Pan** | Select a key and mouse combination for moving the screen. **Zoom** | Select a key and mouse combination for zooming in or out the screen. **Rotate** **(3D Window)** | Select a key and mouse combination for rotating the screen. **Popup Menu** | Select a key and mouse combination for opening the pop-up menu of the 3D Window. **Others** | Axis Constraint Key | Select the key that is used to move items across a constrained horizontal axis, vertical axis, or 45º angle. Smart Panning | Toggle on/off the option to Pan automatically based on the location of the mouse cursor while using certain functions. (Ver .2.5.0) Auto Focus (ver5.0.0) | Toggle on to automatically change the 3D window's focus point based on the user's click. Switch back focus to the default when unselected: The 3D window's focus point returns to all objects when an object is not selected. This option only appears when the **Auto Focus** is toggled ON. **View Point** | Default Y-Axis Position | Set the default position of the Y-Axis. Default X-Axis Position | Set the default position of the X-Axis. Default Camera Distance for Viewpoint Shortcuts (ver4.2.0) | Set the distance between the object and the camera when using the shortcut for view control. Change this setting when the default distance is too far away from the small object. **※ Note:** **Right-Clicks on a MAC** By default, right-clicks are disabled on Macs (Magic Mice, as well as others.) However, the right-click gives you access to important pop-up menus in CLO. You can easily enable right-clicks for your Mac mouse by following the instructions below: 1. Navigate to **System Preferences** (either from your dock or from the Apple menu on the top left hand corner of the screen.) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005447827/______1.png) 2. Select **Mouse**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005496028/______2.png) 3. The **Secondary Click (Click on right side)** option will be unchecked. Check it to enable right-clicks. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005447847/______3.png)

title: Does CLO offer refunds?
content: **Question** Does CLO offer refunds? **Answer** Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds as stated within CLO's Terms of Service agreement. However, in limited cases, **a self-service refund is available within 24 hours of your first billing after a free trial**. You can find more details in this article: [Self-Service Refunds Within 24 Hours of First Billing After Free Trial](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/46600845755161-Self-Service-Refunds-Within-24-Hours-of-First-Billing-After-Free-Trial) Please note that CLO provides auto-renewal subscriptions for individual users, showing a clear notification on the checkout page and asking for your consent before you purchase CLO, as shown below. *Auto-renewal and cancellation policy * Your subscription will automatically renew each billing cycle (monthly or annually, depending on your plan) until canceled. Your selected payment method will be charged at the beginning of each billing period. * You may cancel at any time from your Subscription page to avoid future charges. Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing cycle, and you will retain access to your account until that date. No refunds will be issued for the current billing cycle. * Upon cancellation, you will receive a confirmation email from CLO. If you do not receive a cancellation confirmation email within 24 hours, it is your responsibility to promptly contact CLO to obtain written confirmation. Without such confirmation, your cancellation request will be considered invalid. * Individual users are eligible for a refund within 24 hours of the first billing renewal following the free trial. Refunds can be approved automatically during this 24-hour window. If you receive a refund confirmation email without having requested a refund, or notice any suspicious activity, please contact us immediately. ---
content_description: This page provides essential information regarding CLO's refund policy, including eligibility for self-service refunds within 24 hours of the first billing after a free trial and details about auto-renewal subscriptions.

title: Polygon
content: **List of Contents** Polygon Create Polygon Create Polygon with Curves Create Polygon with Specific Values Create Points in Guidelines Cancel the Last Action Cancel All Actions **Polygon** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uti_3pcl_Tc \- Create Polygon Patterns in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022648248/mceclip0.png) **Polygon** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon.** ** Create Polygon** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6Pi66_PVQQ \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022648248/mceclip0.png) **Polygon** tool and click on the 2D window to draw desired shape of Polygon. \- Click the start point again to complete the Pattern. **Create Polygon with Curves** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7pzr1ZXjZ5Q \- Hold down the Ctrl key while clicking the 2D window to create curves with the free curve point. \- Or, click and drag the mouse while adding a point on the 2D window to create curves with AI Bezier handles. **Create Polygon with Specific Values** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bhp9XaIe_34 \- Click and then right click on the 2D window to access the Create Polygon window. \- Type in the desired value to Length. **Create Points in Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qiaU65EdiU \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to add points in a straight line or a diagonal line. **Cancel the Last Action** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYTWW0AnB34 \- While creating the Polygon Pattern, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action. **Cancel All Actions** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EZYAyQAbwcc \- While creating the Polygon Pattern, hit the Esc or Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard to cancel all actions. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and manipulating polygon patterns in a 2D design environment, featuring video tutorials and step-by-step instructions for various polygon-related tasks.

title: How to enable Auto-pay or E-mandate: Applicable for users with Indian Bank Accounts and Cards.
content: **HDFC Bank**** ** Step 1: **Login** to HDFC Mobile Banking App. Step 2: **Select** ‘Pay’ > **Select** ‘Cards ‘from the main menu. title: Seam Taping
content: **List of Contents** Seam Taping Apply Seam Taping Seam Taping Properties **Seam Taping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PmqyUP9FscA \- Apply Seam Tapes to Pattern outlines to prevent stretch due to gravity. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022652428) **Seam Taping** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials ▶ **Seam Taping.** ** Apply Seam Taping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GoVtcvS9cNs \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022652428) **Seam Taping** tool activated, select the Pattern outline to apply the Seam Tape. \- The segment line with seam tape is highlighted in orange color. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022588847) **Simulation** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- The 3D Garment’s drape will change in the 3D window according to the application. **Seam Taping Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MqIXKWPGRP0 \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022589467) **Edit Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022652428) **Seam Taping** tool to select the desired Seam Tape applied to the Pattern outline. - The selected Seam Tape’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- **Width** : edit the width of the Seam Tape. \- **Preset** : choose the Seam Tape’s preset from the provided options. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on applying seam taping in garment design, including instructional videos and detailed properties for effective use.

title: Fabric_Normal Map
content: **Normal Map ** * **Normal Map ** \- Apply Normal Map images to express uneven texture more realistically. * **Adjust Intensity YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otz3z18Sogk -**Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶ Texture to see its child menus. Then, expand the **Normal Map** option as well. \- Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map using the **Intensity** option. \- When the Normal Map Intensity values is adjusted from 0, CLO will automatically create a Normal Map and express the texture more realistically. * **Apply Normal Map Images YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XuJC92Ksg1w ** * **Via Property Editor** \- The custom made Normal Maps can be applied to the fabric items as well. \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶**** Texture to see its child Menus. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022233407/mceclip0.png)icon next to the Normal Map. The Open File browser will appear. \- Locate the desired Normal Map image and click Open. \- Adjust the intensity values to express the texture more realistically. * **Via Drag & Drop \- **From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop a Normal Map image to the Browser button next to the Normal Map option. * **Apply with Desired Map Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ka8kOCuOpGM ****-** From the PC’s Browser window, drag and drop an image file to an object where the image should be applied to. \- The Texture Map Type window appears. Choose the desired Map type and select OK. * Save Auto-generated Normal Map YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=35_-fG1DxC4 \- Normal Map generated when adjusting Intensity can now be saved. \- Adjust the Intensity under the Normal Map option. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶Surface Textures and locate the saving path. \- Select Original size or Crop size when saving. \- The Normal Map can be saved when exporting as OBJ,FBX,LXO. **※** Note: Normal Map and Roughness Map are retained even if Texture is deleted.(ver.4.2)
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions and resources for applying and adjusting Normal Map images to achieve realistic texture on fabric items in your 3D modeling projects.
